ops.old: A record number of ACOs participated in the Medicare Shared Savings Program in performance year 2024.
ops.new: In performance year 2024, 476 ACOs participated in the Medicare Shared Savings Program, and the highest share of ACOs since the program began earned performance payments.
ops.claim: "A record number of ACOs participated" in PY2024
ops.sources: CMS fact sheet "Medicare Shared Savings Program ACOs Updated Performance Year 2024 Financial and Quality Results" (2025-09-29): 476 ACOs; 75% earning $4.1B; 10.3M assigned; Medicare saved $2.5B; $245 net / $651 gross per capita; highest share earning and highest savings since inception; low-revenue $319 vs high-revenue $180; BP 77.80% -> 79.49%; MSSP peaked at 561 ACOs in 2018 (CMS Fast Facts)
ops.note: 476 is well below the 2018 peak; CMS's record was the share earning payments.

ops.old: MSSP ACOs generated $2.4 billion in net savings to Medicare in performance year 2024, a new program record.
ops.new: Medicare saved $2.5 billion relative to ACO benchmarks in performance year 2024, the highest since the program began.

ops.old: Under the "Pathways to Success" redesign finalized in 2018, CMS reduced the maximum time an ACO can remain in upside-only risk from six years to two years for most ACOs, with an extension to three years for low-revenue (typically physician-led) ACOs.
ops.new: The "Pathways to Success" redesign finalized in 2018 sharply shortened the time an ACO could remain in upside-only risk, but CMS later loosened that limit: the CY2023 Physician Fee Schedule rule let eligible ACOs stay upside-only for up to seven performance years, and in the CY2026 rulemaking CMS moved to cut the maximum back to five.
ops.claim: Pathways cut upside-only time from 6 to 2 years (3 for low-revenue) — stated as current
ops.sources: CMS fact sheet "Medicare Shared Savings Program ACOs Updated Performance Year 2024 Financial and Quality Results" (2025-09-29): 476 ACOs; 75% earning $4.1B; 10.3M assigned; Medicare saved $2.5B; $245 net / $651 gross per capita; highest share earning and highest savings since inception; low-revenue $319 vs high-revenue $180; BP 77.80% -> 79.49% (CY2026 PFS proposal: one-sided BASIC limited to 5 years "instead of a maximum of 7 performance years"); CMS Pathways to Success fact sheet (Dec 2018)
ops.note: Stated as current policy though reversed by the CY2023 rule.

ops.old: In 2024, two-thirds of MSSP ACOs were operating in the Level E or ENHANCED track, meaning the majority of the program now carries downside risk. This is a marked shift from the program's early years, when nearly all ACOs stayed in upside-only tracks indefinitely. High-risk-track ACOs generated more than two-thirds of all net savings in 2024—$5.4 billion of the $6.6 billion total gross savings—demonstrating that financial accountability correlates with stronger performance.
ops.new: A growing share of MSSP ACOs now carries downside risk — a marked shift from the program's early years, when nearly all ACOs stayed in upside-only tracks. Performance in 2024 also varied by organization type: low-revenue ACOs, typically physician-led or built around FQHCs and rural health clinics, generated $319 in net per capita savings versus $180 for high-revenue, typically hospital-led ACOs, and ACOs composed predominantly of primary care clinicians generated $403 versus $224.
ops.claim: Two-thirds of ACOs in Level E/ENHANCED in 2024; high-risk ACOs $5.4B of $6.6B gross savings
ops.sources: CMS fact sheet "Medicare Shared Savings Program ACOs Updated Performance Year 2024 Financial and Quality Results" (2025-09-29): 476 ACOs; 75% earning $4.1B; 10.3M assigned; Medicare saved $2.5B; $245 net / $651 gross per capita; highest share earning and highest savings since inception; low-revenue $319 vs high-revenue $180; BP 77.80% -> 79.49%
ops.note: Neither figure appears in CMS PY2024 results; replaced with CMS-published comparisons.

ops.claim: ENHANCED track "eligible for additional investment payments"
ops.sources: CMS CY2023 PFS final rule: advance investment payments limited to new, inexperienced, low-revenue ACOs entering the BASIC track
